children: Actor-filmmaker
Ben Affleck
pushed back against fears that artificial intelligence (AI) will eliminate large numbers of jobs or take control of the entertainment industry, calling some of the most extreme concerns "propaganda."

In an interview with Bloomberg on Thursday at Bloomberg Screentime 2026 in Los Angeles, Affleck discussed AI’s role in filmmaking, his experience developing AI tools, and why he believes the technology is more likely to supplement creative work than replace it.
Affleck Says AI Can Add To Hollywood

Affleck said filmmakers often become less fearful of AI once they understand how the technology actually works and can use it themselves. He compared the shift to earlier technological advances in filmmaking, arguing that AI can become another tool rather than an autonomous force capable of taking over the industry.
Affleck said AI is already being used on films without reducing staffing levels. "In fact, more people technically are being employed," he said. Affleck said he believes
Netflix, Inc.
has been judicious in its use of AI and is focused on improving filmmaking rather than simply cutting costs.

Affleck said AI was used in Animals, primarily in post-production, where it helped the production move faster and complete some work that otherwise may not have been possible. He declined to detail every application, saying revealing too much could undermine the illusion created for audiences.

children: ‘I Don’t Worry About Skynet’

Affleck said his concerns about AI extend to his children’s education, including what he described as a rise in college grades and the risk of ‘learned helplessness,’ if people become overly dependent on technology.
"I don’t worry about Skynet," Affleck said, adding that he expects AI to be "additive" to the filmmaking business rather than take it over.
